title: ‘Feeble and frail’ Jerry Sandusky makes first public appearance since 2019 for hearing
content:
BELLEFONTE, Pa. — A visibly gaunt Jerry Sandusky made his first public appearance since 2019 on Tuesday, appearing via Zoom in a courtroom in central Pennsylvania for an evidentiary hearing concerning the testimony of one of the accusers in his 2012 conviction on 45 counts of sexual abuse.

The hearing, which lasted about 40 minutes, was centered on a claim that one of Sandusky’s accusers, recognized in court documents at R.R., or Victim 10, sought to recant his testimony from the trial. Attorneys for the former Penn State football assistant tried to withdraw from the hearing last week, but Judge Maureen Skerda said the hearing would proceed and allowed Sandusky to appear remotely.

Sandusky’s attorney, Jerry Russo, said after the hearing that his client’s aim is to seek a new trial at a higher court.

The 82-year-old Sandusky is in custody at minimum-security Laurel Highlands, a state correctional facility in Somerset, Pa., where is serving a lengthy sentence. He offered mostly one-word answers to questions from Skerda and prosecutors. His voice sounded shaky and diffident at times, and it was difficult to hear on multiple occasions. He wore a brown button-down shirt and sat with his shoulders slouched in an armless beige chair at a wooden table. With visibly less hair than his last public appearance, Sandusky struggled to hear Skerda through the video link and repeatedly apologized when asking for questions to be repeated.

“He’s got heart issues. He’s delayed a heart surgery. He’s 82 years of age, you saw him if you were in the courtroom,” Russo said outside the courthouse after the hearing. “He’s feeble and frail.”

When asked about Sandusky’s demeanor, Russo answered: “Prayerful.”

The screen displaying Sandusky was positioned at the front right of the courtroom, to the left of Skerda’s bench. His wife, Dottie, sat nearby.

She watched the screen intently, her hands pressed against her face for much of the hearing. On multiple occasions, she could be heard whispering her husband’s answers as Sandusky struggled to hear. Walking with a cane, she went up to Russo after the court was adjourned and placed a hand on his left arm.

There were multiple supporters of Sandusky in the courtroom, two of whom embraced afterward. One of the former coach’s supporters, who described himself as a personal friend of Sandusky’s, spoke with a group of reporters after the hearing and handed out a copy of an open letter written to talk-show host Megyn Kelly.
